- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 7–14 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +10% above peak for next 5 days.  
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (first 3–5 days drop > 5% from peak), model overreacts; adjust downward by 2–5% in next 3–7 days.  
- When sentiment swings from negative to positive (e.g., +0.3+ in 2–3 days), model delays correction; add 1–3 days lag in downward adjustment.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if history shows strong downward trend (avg < 75) and sentiment negative, model often underestimates; add 2–5% upward bias.  
- If forecast and true outcome diverge > 10% in first 3 days, sentiment is a better predictor than price history; use sentiment as primary signal for next 5 days.
